passage: Archaeologists are using advanced imaging technologies to explore ancient structures without disturbing them. Ground-penetrating radar, for example, sends radio waves into the earth and measures their reflections, allowing researchers to identify buried walls or chambers. This method is especially valuable at historical sites where excavation could damage fragile artifacts. In recent years, archaeologists have combined radar with aerial lidar, which maps the surface by measuring how quickly laser pulses return to sensors. When the two techniques are used together, scientists can create detailed 3D models of entire settlements. These models reveal patterns in city planning, trade activity, and cultural practices. Although the technology is costly and requires specialized training, it allows researchers to uncover information that might otherwise remain hidden. As imaging tools become more accessible, they are likely to play an increasingly important role in preserving archaeological sites across the world.
